title: Birbal and the Donkey
summary: Jealous courtiers try to insult Birbal by comparing him to a donkey. Birbal turns the joke upon them with effortless wit.
full_text:
During a festival procession in Agra, Emperor Akbar, Birbal, and several high-ranking courtiers were riding their horses through the crowded streets. A stray donkey happened to cross the road, braying loudly at the royal procession.

A courtier named Nawab Asif Khan, who harbored deep envy toward Birbal, saw an opportunity to humiliate him before the Emperor.

Asif Khan pointed at the braying donkey, turned to Birbal with a mocking sneer, and asked: 'Tell me, Raja Birbal, what is your relation to that noisy animal? He seems to be calling out to you as if he recognized his brother!'

The other courtiers snickered, waiting to see Birbal squirm.

Birbal remained completely composed. He looked at the donkey, then turned to Nawab Asif Khan with polite, affectionate warmth:

'Nawab Sahib, he is indeed a distant relative of mine—a relative by marriage! You see, he is my brother-in-law on your side of the family!'

The entire street erupted in laughter. Nawab Asif Khan's face turned purple, and he hung his head in mortified silence.

Emperor Akbar chuckled into his sleeve and whispered: 'Never throw stones at a man who lives in a fortress of wit, Asif Khan, for his arrows never miss their mark!'
